A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same kNNSampler work and have readable text, equations, figures and appendices. Experimental material in v1 Appendix B can be matched to v2's main-text tables.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original synthetic experiments measuring distribution recovery, RMSE and prediction-interval coverage.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original synthetic results, and Section 5 adds original experiments on solar-power data.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 still samples uniformly from the responses of the k nearest observed covariates. The conditional-distribution estimator, MSE-based cross-validation for k, uncertainty estimates and multiple-imputation procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates two synthetic models: linear responses with chi-square noise and a noisy ring. V2 retains both and adds a real solar-panel dataset containing 67,698 irradiation/DC-power pairs, substantially extending coverage beyond simulations.

E2.justification: The matched synthetic comparisons retain Linear Imputation, Random Forest, kNNImputer and kNN×KDE. V2's solar benchmark uses the same comparator set; the newly cited solar studies are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5 adds a solar-specific protocol using subsets of 10,000–60,000 pairs and masking 30% of units with irradiation between 0.4 and 0.6, plus a full-dataset visualization. Existing synthetic sample sizes, masking rules and baseline configurations are retained.

E4.justification: V2 Figure 6 adds a qualitative solar-data case study examining whether imputations preserve heterogeneous variability and non-negativity. The prediction-interval coverage analysis is unchanged, and the existing RMSE comparison is relocated from Appendix B rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 removes the permutation two-sample testing procedure and p-value reporting from v1 Section 4.1.2 and Figures 7–8. Both versions retain means and standard deviations over 10 independent runs; the solar experiments use that same reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial real-data results in Table 5 and Figure 6. At 60,000 solar observations, reported energy distances are 0.148 ± 0.077 for kNNSampler and 1.927 ± 0.942 for kNN×KDE. These are new benchmark results, not cross-version performance gains. Synthetic energy-distance and RMSE results are retained in tables, while p-value result series are removed.

T1.justification: Equation 12 corrects the bias exponent from d/2 to 2/d, consistent with Theorem 1. Appendix A.2 replaces an invalid cancellation in the bounded-difference argument with an explicit triangle-inequality derivation using A, A' and B. The theorem, assumptions and claimed convergence rate remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim conditional-distribution estimation, consistency and convergence rates governed by intrinsic dimension, with applications to uncertainty quantification and multiple imputation. The abstract's softer experimental wording and additional real-data support do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning low-dimensional evaluation, distance-function choice, MSE-based selection of k and unestablished downstream uncertainty calibration. Remarks 1–2 explain deterministic imputation's overconfidence from a Bayesian perspective. Section 5 interprets solar-data failure mechanisms, while v1's p-value-based argument for greater stability is removed.

D1.justification: Section 5 supplies a solar-dataset access link, identifies the covariate and response, and describes subset and missingness construction. Existing code access, cross-validation information and synthetic baseline hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Murray (2018) and Rubin (1996) for multiple imputation, Peyré et al. (2019) for the metric discussion, and Costa et al. (2024) and Phan et al. (2023) for solar applications. Positioning relative to hot-deck methods, kNN×KDE and conditional mean embeddings remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 adds explanatory remarks, revises the quantitative-results discussion, separates synthetic and real-data experiments, and expands the conclusion into a discussion with limitations. Appendix B's discussion is incorporated into the main text. Most existing method and theory prose remains intact.

P2.justification: V1's energy-distance and RMSE plots become v2 Tables 1–4, including results previously in Appendix B. The duplicate close-up energy plots and p-value plots disappear, coverage Figure 9 becomes Figure 5, and solar Figure 6 and Table 5 are added. This substantially redesigns the empirical presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical reliability through the Equation 12 correction and repaired Appendix A.2 argument. The solar study adds practical evidence, explicit limitations better qualify applicability, and numerical tables make results easier to inspect. These provide a limited net improvement: the new application remains low-dimensional, and removing permutation-test results reduces statistical detail, although the main distance, RMSE and coverage evidence is retained.
